newsitem.title: SPAIN: US, Spain farm groups want check on altered seeds.
newsitem.headline: US, Spain farm groups want check on altered seeds.

text.p: A U.S. farmers' group joined forces with Spanish farmers on Thursday to call for a "reality check" on gene-altered seeds which they say pose serious dangers to humans and the environment.

"We certainly should not allow products with altered genes into the environment until we have conclusive knowledge about their long-term effects...We call on on the USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) and the administration to make a reality check on biotechnology," said Bill Christison of U.S-based National Family Farm Coalition.
The groups are protesting at gene-modified soybean and maize seeds, manufactured by firms such as Ciba-Geigy and Monsanto Co and designed to be resistant to some pests and pesticides.

"Many family farmers are alarmed at the prospects of having the seed stocks owned and patented by a corporation, especially when that corporation is the same one that sells the chemicals that are necessary for production of the crop," Cristison said.
Spain's Agriculture Ministry is planning to include Ciba-Geigy gene-modified grains in its official seeds catalogue, according to agricultural association COAG.
"We are surprised and worried at this decision...(which) could endanger public health and the environment," COAG said in a letter to Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio.
The groups called for the withdrawal of the products until adequate testing could be done.
